title: SQL-like queries over CSV files
spec:
The repository is empty. Create `csvq.py` with `run(sql)` that executes one query over a CSV file and returns the result as a string, and `class QueryError(Exception)` raised for every invalid query.

Grammar (keywords and function names are case-insensitive; column names are case-sensitive and match the header exactly; tokens are separated by optional whitespace):

    SELECT select_list FROM path [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY col {, col}] [ORDER BY key [ASC|DESC] {, key [ASC|DESC]}] [LIMIT n]

- `path`: a run of characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_./-]`, opened relative to the current directory. Read it with Python's `csv` module (default dialect); the first row is the header. Missing file -> QueryError.
- `select_list`: `*` (all columns in file order) or a comma-separated list of items, each a column name or an aggregate: `COUNT(*)`, `COUNT(col)`, `SUM(col)`, `AVG(col)`, `MIN(col)`, `MAX(col)`.
- Column names in queries match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and are never keywords. Unknown column -> QueryError.
- `expr`, lowest to highest precedence: `OR`, `AND`, `NOT` (prefix, may repeat), then a predicate. A predicate is `( expr )`, `operand op operand` with op one of `= != <> < <= > >=`, or `operand IS NULL` / `operand IS NOT NULL`. An operand is a column name, a number literal (`-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?`) or a string literal in single quotes where `''` stands for one quote (`'O''Brien'`). `NULL` appears only in `IS [NOT] NULL`.
- `n` is a non-negative integer. Anything left over or out of place (e.g. trailing tokens, unterminated strings) -> QueryError.

Values and types:
- A cell that is the empty string is NULL. Cells are not trimmed.
- A column is numeric if all of its non-NULL cells match `-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` (a column with no non-NULL cells is numeric); otherwise it is a string column and every value in it is a string. Numbers compare numerically, strings by Python's default string ordering.
- Comparing a number with a string (numeric column or number literal vs string column or string literal) -> QueryError, raised even if no row is evaluated.

NULL semantics (SQL three-valued logic): a comparison with a NULL operand is UNKNOWN. `NOT UNKNOWN` is UNKNOWN; `FALSE AND UNKNOWN` is FALSE, `TRUE AND UNKNOWN` is UNKNOWN; `TRUE OR UNKNOWN` is TRUE, `FALSE OR UNKNOWN` is UNKNOWN. WHERE keeps only rows where the expression is TRUE. `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` are never UNKNOWN.

Aggregation:
- A query aggregates if it has GROUP BY or any aggregate in its select list. With GROUP BY, every plain column in the select list must be one of the GROUP BY columns and `*` is not allowed (QueryError otherwise); there is one output row per distinct combination of GROUP BY values (NULLs group together), in order of first appearance among the WHERE-filtered rows; no rows -> no groups. Without GROUP BY, an aggregating select list must contain only aggregates and the query returns exactly one row, even over zero rows.
- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; the other aggregates ignore NULLs. `COUNT(col)` counts non-NULL values. `SUM`/`AVG` require a numeric column (QueryError otherwise). `MIN`/`MAX` work on both types. With no non-NULL input, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX` are NULL and `COUNT` is 0.

ORDER BY:
- In a non-aggregating query a key is any column of the file (selected or not). In an aggregating query a key is a GROUP BY column or an aggregate expression as above (selected or not); anything else -> QueryError.
- Sorting compares keys left to right; NULL sorts before every value in ASC (the default) and after every value in DESC. Rows equal on all keys keep their input order (file order, or group first-appearance order) in both directions. LIMIT applies after sorting.

Output: CSV text produced by `csv.writer` with `lineterminator="\n"`: a header row then one row per result row (so the string ends with a newline). Header names: the column name, or for an aggregate the upper-case function name followed by `(col)` or `(*)` with no spaces, e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `SUM(price)`, whatever spacing or case the query used. Values: NULL -> empty field; a column value (and the result of MIN/MAX) -> the original cell text; COUNT -> an integer; SUM and AVG -> computed exactly with `decimal.Decimal` from the cell texts, rounded to 6 decimal places with ROUND_HALF_UP, then printed without trailing zeros or a trailing point (`4`, `1.5`, `0.333333`, `-2.25`; zero is `0`).

Example: with `t.csv` = `name,qty\na,3\nb,\na,4\n`, `run("select name, sum(qty) from t.csv group by name order by SUM(qty) desc")` returns `"name,SUM(qty)\na,7\nb,\n"`.

Add unit tests runnable with `python3 -m unittest -q`.
acceptance: the grammar, precedence and literal rules work as specified
column typing, NULL three-valued logic and aggregate NULL handling follow the spec
GROUP BY, ORDER BY (NULL placement, stable ties) and LIMIT interact correctly
output CSV, header names and number formatting are exact
